description: Concepts, history, techniques, and applications of AI

entries.definition: AI is the simulation of human intelligence processes by machines, especially computer systems, including learning, reasoning, and self-correction.

history.1950: Alan Turing proposes Turing Test in 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence'
history.1956: Dartmouth Conference; term 'Artificial Intelligence' coined by John McCarthy
history.1966: ELIZA chatbot created at MIT; first natural language processing program
history.1997: IBM Deep Blue defeats chess world champion Garry Kasparov
history.2011: IBM Watson wins Jeopardy! against human champions
history.2012: AlexNet wins ImageNet; deep learning breakthrough
history.2016: AlphaGo defeats Go world champion Lee Sedol
history.2022: ChatGPT released; large language models go mainstream
history.2023: GPT-4, Claude, Gemini; multimodal AI systems emerge

types_of_ai.narrow_ai: AI designed for specific tasks (current AI); e.g., image recognition, translation
types_of_ai.general_ai: AI with human-level intelligence across all domains; not yet achieved
types_of_ai.superintelligence: Hypothetical AI surpassing human intelligence in all respects

machine_learning_types.supervised_learning: Model trains on labeled data; learns input-output mappings
machine_learning_types.unsupervised_learning: Model finds patterns in unlabeled data; clustering, dimensionality reduction
machine_learning_types.reinforcement_learning: Agent learns by interacting with environment; maximizes reward
machine_learning_types.semi_supervised: Mix of labeled and unlabeled data
machine_learning_types.self_supervised: Model generates its own supervision signal from data

deep_learning.neural_networks: Layers of interconnected nodes (neurons) inspired by the brain
deep_learning.cnn: Convolutional Neural Networks; excel at image recognition
deep_learning.rnn: Recurrent Neural Networks; designed for sequential data
deep_learning.lstm: Long Short-Term Memory; solves vanishing gradient problem in RNNs
deep_learning.transformer: Attention-based architecture; basis of modern LLMs (2017)
deep_learning.gan: Generative Adversarial Networks; generator vs discriminator; creates synthetic data

large_language_models.definition: Deep learning models trained on massive text corpora to understand and generate language
large_language_models.training: Pre-training on huge datasets, fine-tuning with RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback)

ai_ethics.bias: AI systems can reflect and amplify human biases present in training data
ai_ethics.privacy: Large data requirements raise surveillance concerns
ai_ethics.alignment: Ensuring AI systems act according to human values and intentions
ai_ethics.safety: Preventing catastrophic or unintended AI behavior
